title: Canada adds Masar Badil group to terrorist entity list, citing status as alias for Samidoun
summary: Canada's public safety minister announced Monday that Masar Badil had been added to the country's terrorist entity list, as an alias for Samidoun, a group which was added to the same list in 2024.

blocks.text: Canada's public safety minister announced Monday that Masar Badil had been added to the country's terrorist entity list, as an alias for Samidoun, a group which was added to the same list in 2024.
Samidoun was added to list 2 years ago

In a news release, Public Safety Canada said "there is evidence" that Masar Badil — also known as the Palestinian Alternative Revolutionary Path Movement — and Samidoun "are the same entity" and "Masar Badil is acting as a faction/offshoot of Samidoun."

Public Safety Canada describes Masar Badil as an international movement "that claims to be working to build solidarity with Palestinian prisoners," but which operates under "the umbrella movement of Samidoun," which the government says the group has acknowledged having links to.
Samidoun and Masar Badil also have shared leadership and participate in joint events, according to the government.
Ottawa added Samidoun to the terrorist entity list two years ago, in a joint action with the U.S.

The U.S., meanwhile, imposed sanctions on Masar Badil earlier this year. The state-side action saw officials also assert that the group is "inextricably linked" with Samidoun.

Several news outlets, including Global News and the National Post, reported Ottawa's move to list Masar Badil comes days before a conference organized by the group was scheduled to take place in Toronto.
The Public Safety Canada news release did not make mention of the pending conference.
Provides additional tools to law enforcement

Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree said in a statement Monday that the move to put Masar Badil on the list of terrorist entities, as an alias for Samidoun, will provide law enforcement with additional tools "to disrupt their financing, dismantle their networks, hold their members accountable, and to protect all people in Canada from terrorism and organized violence."
The Public Safety Canada news release said that a group that is put on the terrorist entity list then meets "the definition of a 'terrorist group' under Canada’s Criminal Code."

The Criminal Code, in turn, prohibits certain actions in relation to such groups, "including those related to terrorist financing, travel and recruitment," Public Safety Canada said in its news release.

The Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs said in a published statement that it welcomed Ottawa's action on Masar Badil, but said the government had more work to do " to close gaps and enforce Canada’s anti-terrorism legislation."
